informativeness.headline: At every horizon K=1..10 the k-step probability predicts the CURRENT label A(t) at least as well as the future label A(t+k), and the gap widens monotonically with K. The rollout behaves as a nowcast that scores well on the future because the label persists, not as a forecast.

horizon_status.practical_operating_horizon_note: Numerical stability alone does not make a horizon useful. See informativeness.per_horizon: the incremental AUC over a pure nowcast is negative at EVERY horizon and worsens monotonically, so no horizon in K=1..10 is demonstrated to carry forecasting information beyond a description of the present.

limitations: PROVENANCE, INHERITED NOT RESOLVED: the frozen V4 checkpoint was trained on the single-day temporal_benchmark_v2 arrays but is evaluated here on multiday_benchmark_K5 arrays scaled by a different StandardScaler. Every number in this task inherits that mismatch (docs/v4_baseline_manifest.json known_issues). This experiment does not repair it and does not resolve it.
The test split is a SINGLE day (Friday-02-03-2018) with only 3 observable attack onsets, so every early-warning figure is anecdotal rather than an estimate.
Transition-conditioned statistics rest on 3 to 12 onsets and 3 to 12 offsets. They are reported because the direction of the effect is consistent, but no individual value is statistically reliable.
Aggregate metrics at large K are dominated by label persistence (99.2% at K=10), not by forecasting skill. Reading ROC-AUC alone across horizons is misleading.
The F1 series across K is NOT like-for-like: K=1,2,3,5 use frozen thresholds and K=4,6..10 use validation-selected exploratory thresholds.

Ground truth for K=6..10 was reconstructed from the same states_v2 source the benchmark was built from; 10 of 3,115 sequences lack a contiguous K=10 target and are excluded at that horizon rather than imputed.

The stability boundary is defined relative to each quantity's own K=1 value, so it measures DEGRADATION WITH HORIZON. It says nothing about whether V4 is good in absolute terms — and on the state-decoder arm it is not (see forecast_error.csv).
